title: Nobody caused it alone
lines: A man sits outside in the cold while everyone explains why someone else should help.
Responsibility argues that what we owe depends on our ability to help, as well as who caused the harm.
The people who caused a problem, can repair it, and should prevent it may all be different.

emotionalPlan.purpose: Distinguish blame, repair and prevention when deciding what a person or institution owes.
emotionalPlan.visualActing: Open on the cold doorway and hesitant residents, using restrained posture instead of accusation.
voiceDirections: Quiet compassion; gently emphasize “in the cold”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.
Clear and warmly interested; give a small emphasis to “ability to help”, then finish at an ordinary conversational pace without a dramatic rise.
Patient distinction; gently emphasize “all be different”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

title: Blame is only one question
lines: The book follows these different duties through ordinary encounters and failures inside institutions.
It asks how power and vulnerability change what we owe, and where one person’s ability to help ends.
How can a demand remain fair without letting the powerful pretend there is nothing they can do?

title: The reach of an obligation
lines: Knowing whose fault it was can still leave a person waiting for help.
Return to the doorway, and ask which question might change what happens next.
